Mayo Clinic News Network, "Covid Queries: Altered DNA and microchips", October 11, 2021, states that there is absolutely no microchip in the COVID-19 vaccine and no way for the vaccine to track people or gather personal information. This myth originated from comments made by Bill Gates about a digital certificate of vaccine records, which was not a microchip and not tied to vaccine development or distribution. [1]
Mosaic Life Care, "Debunking COVID-19 myths", states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are made only with ingredients that help the body recognize and clear out the virus. [2]
The CDC Archive, "Myths and Facts about COVID-19 Vaccines", February 16, 2023, confirms that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are developed to fight disease, not to track movement. [3]
Mayo Clinic, "Debunking COVID-19 myths", August 30, 2026, reiterates that COVID-19 vaccines do not have microchips and are composed of ingredients that help the body fight the virus. [4]
The Wellness Coalition, "Do COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips?", March 26, 2023, states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are designed to stimulate the immune system. [5]
Komdigi, "Vaksin Covid-19 Punya Chip untuk Lacak Orang? Itu Disinformasi!", states that the claim of COVID-19 vaccines containing chips to track people is false. The barcode on vaccine products is for tracking product distribution, not for tracking individuals. [6]
